clue.text: Light roof rack bar not hard to bend for Barbary apes here

indicators.note: bending the letters out of shape rearranges them into a new order
not having something means it is removed from the letters

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone describes a light rooftop rack that bends, oddly destined for monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' drops H from LIGHT ROOF RACK BAR, and 'to bend' rearranges the remaining fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbary macaques living on Gibraltar's famous limestone promontory are Europe's only wild monkeys.

clue.text: Cancelled vicar sanctioned

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar
to OK something is to approve it, so OK'd means sanctioned

explanation.surface: A vicar has been cancelled, and someone in authority approved it.
explanation.definitionFit: Revoked is a synonym of cancelled, as with a licence or permission withdrawn.

clue.text: Vehicle type lacking large body

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: lacking means the letter is missing from the word

parts.note: a class is a type or kind
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A vehicle of some kind has no big body, as if describing a small car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass is a dead body, usually of an animal.

clue.text: In amongst reformed Ocean Colour Scene for an Apollo appearance — it doesn't happen often

indicators.note: amongst places the small word between the letters of the other piece
reformed means formed again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
blue is a colour
the Apollo missions landed astronauts on the Moon

explanation.surface: It seems to describe the band Ocean Colour Scene reuniting for a rare gig at a venue called the Apollo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour' and 'Scene' are not part of the band's name here but separate pieces. Ocean Colour Scene is a British rock band; the Hammersmith Apollo is a London venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something extremely rare, a phenomenon that hardly ever occurs.

clue.text: Example of wishing well with gunge on left to get eaten by bird

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: goo is gunge, sticky mess

indicators.note: being eaten by something puts the letter inside that word

parts.note: a duck is a bird

explanation.surface: A wishing well left covered in gunge is being pecked at by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wishing well' is not the fountain: the phrase means hoping things go well for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it to someone is a typical way to express hope that their venture succeeds.

clue.text: For Spooner, chuck rock cake in famous tea party location

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: to toss is to chuck or throw
a rock cake is a kind of bun

explanation.surface: Someone is throwing a hard rock cake at a famous historical tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: TOSS BUN with first sounds swapped is BOSS TUN, said like the city. A rock cake is a rough-surfaced British bun.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1773 colonists dumped British tea into the harbour of that Massachusetts city in protest at taxation.

clue.text: Her outfit was of a strange type that doesn't really fit

indicators.note: strange letters are odd and out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Her clothes were peculiar, of a style that did not suit her or hang right.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings, out of their element.

clue.text: In retirement drunk cut excess

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so in a down clue the word goes upward, backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunk
to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: In retirement a heavy drinker cut back on overindulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over, more than needed, is spare or surplus: in excess.

clue.text: Landlord installs electronic log again

indicators.note: the landlord puts something inside, so the letter goes within the word

parts.note: a renter can be one who lets out property for rent
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A landlord fits an electronic log, perhaps a fake fire, in a rented flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log' is the verb, as in recording data.
explanation.definitionFit: To log data again is to input it a second time, to key it in once more.

clue.text: Famous punk's first single covered by old artist, taking in a great deal

indicators.note: covered by means hidden and replaced, so the first single letter gives way to the new ones

parts.note: Sid Vicious was the bassist of the Sex Pistols
I is the Roman numeral one, a single; the first of two in the name is changed
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A punk star's first single was covered by an old-school artist and made a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' looks like a music cover version; it means the first I of VICIOUS is replaced by O and RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A voracious eater consumes huge quantities, being greedy or insatiable.

clue.text: Spacecraft with unlimited fuel supply

parts.note: ISS is the International Space Station

indicators.note: without its limits the word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A spacecraft with endless fuel supply, a science-fiction dream.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue goods is to hand them out or distribute them.

clue.text: Bog seen through murk hazily

indicators.note: letters glimpsed through other words are inside them

explanation.surface: A marsh is glimpsed dimly through the gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' looks like a marsh in this misty scene; it is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for a lavatory, the second the more vulgar.

clue.text: Brave sort, 51, running and dirt cycling

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
a machine that is running is on

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: earth is dirt or soil

explanation.surface: A tough fifty-one-year-old goes running and cycling on dirt trails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the H of EARTH from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with great courage, like Richard I, is called brave as a lion.

clue.text: Range of papers backing policy

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: ID, identity documents, are papers
a stance is a position or policy

explanation.surface: A spread of newspapers supports a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's range is the distance it can reach.

clue.text: Perhaps Bergman's included when Truffaut meets Europeans

indicators.note: only the letters included at the tail of the director's name are kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: Eur is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Bergman joins in when the French director Truffaut meets fellow European filmmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meets' joins the tail of Truffaut to the abbreviation. The answer is a film director with a distinctive personal vision, a term Truffaut himself championed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingmar Bergman, the Swedish film-maker, is a classic example of a director with a personal style.

clue.text: Essentially brew in teapot, stirring for show

indicators.note: stirring mixes up, so the letters are rearranged
the essence of a word is its central part, its middle letters

explanation.surface: Brewing tea properly requires stirring the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light comic opera, a stage show.

clue.text: Capricious film student's going to finish scene at last

indicators.note: the letter goes to the end of the word

parts.note: a flick is a film
L is a learner driver, a student; 's here means is

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A film student is about to finish the final scene of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: A fickle person changes their mind on a whim, unpredictably.

clue.text: Floating wreckage — start to find loads before noon

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

parts.note: lots means loads, a great many
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: Beachcombers find heaps of driftwood early in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris from a shipwreck that drifts on the sea surface.

clue.text: Dictator's arrest of Russian playwright

indicators.note: dictating is speaking for someone to write down, so this tells us the words are said aloud

parts.note: to check is to arrest or halt; taken as written

explanation.surface: A tyrant has a Russian dramatist detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant; it means one who dictates, speaking words aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov wrote The Cherry Orchard and The Seagull.

clue.text: Just a bit of fun swimming in small pool

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: swimming letters move about in the water, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small paddling pool gives only a little enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoonful is a small amount, only as much as a spoon holds.

clue.text: Surfacing material to be used on motorway roughly

parts.note: something intended for a use is for it
the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, its 1 read as the letter I
ca, circa, means roughly or about

explanation.surface: Road surfacing to be laid approximately on a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough plastic laminate brand used to cover kitchen worktops.

clue.text: Way to store dip in dish

indicators.note: storing keeps something inside, so the letters go within

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
a sag is a dip

explanation.surface: Instructions for keeping a dip in a serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked pasta dish.

clue.text: Visit Uruguay regularly — heading north to make matches

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: to see a doctor is to visit one

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: Travel advice: visit Uruguay often, heading north to watch football matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that tally or correspond are said to agree.

clue.text: More than base rate's introduction on maturity — too ambitious?

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: over means more than
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics
age is maturity

indicators.note: the introduction of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A financial query about interest above the base rate on a maturing investment.
explanation.definitionFit: An overeager person is excessively keen, pushing too hard.

clue.text: Factory farms?

definitions.meaning: a plant or factory, as in steelworks
to farm land is to work it, so farms means tills

explanation.definitionFit: An industrial plant is a works, and someone who farms land works it.

clue.text: Chump in US school has way of doing things

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A fool in an American school has his own method.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang from Yiddish for a stupid or contemptible person.

clue.text: Calling hospital department — how's your father feeling without iron tablet?

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
British slang for sex, which crosswords also call it

indicators.note: without means these letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
E is an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Phoning a hospital department about odd feelings from a missing iron supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing FE and E from FEELING leaves LING. 'How's your father' is jokey British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book is to give it a name, to call it something.

clue.text: Most AA servicing defective for powered flight

indicators.note: defective things are faulty, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Breakdown servicing by the AA is mostly faulty, bad news for engines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is not air travel but a flight of stairs. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a staircase with motor-driven steps, a flight of stairs run by power.
